solution.p: Both of these equations are written in standard form. The first equation, x-3y=-12\text{,} has x-intercept at (-12,0) and y-intercept at (0,4)\text{.} The second equation, x+y=-4\text{,} has x-intercept at (-4,0) and y-intercept at (0,-4)\text{.} We can use this information to graph both lines.

image.shortdescription: a Cartesian grid with two intersecting lines; one line has a x-intercept of -12 and y-intercept of 4; the other line has x-intercept of -4 and y-intercept of -4

solution.p: It appears that the two lines intersect where x=-6 and y=2\text{,} so the solution to the system of equations would be the point (-6,2)\text{.} However we should check that (-6,2) actually works as a solution to each of the original equations. \begin{aligned} x-3y\amp=-12\amp x+y\amp=-4\\ \substitute{-6}-3(\substitute{2})\amp\wonder{=}-12\amp \substitute{-6}+\substitute{2}\amp\wonder{=}-4\\ -6-6\amp\confirm{=}-12\amp -4\amp\confirm{=}-4 \end{aligned} This verifies that (-6,2) is the solution.
